messages:
jordana: Morning — ran anchor-set priming sweep (3 anchor sets) vs control on the new 3B reranker-int8 build. Quick heads-up: ndcg@10 drop on anchor-set B vs control ~0.012, mrr up slightly.

sam: Can you paste the eval command and seed? also which quant profile?

jordana: eval command: `python eval.py --model r3b-v2-int8 --anchors anchors_B.json --seed 42 --batch 512`
Quant profile: `mix-q4_0` (per-layer hybrid).

mike: curious if anchor B has more long queries? distribution looks shifted to >120 tokens.

jordana: yes — anchors_B.json is heavy on longform. I clipped docs to 512 but queries average 140. suspect kv-cache truncation + priming tokens causing context bleed.

dina: Did you try unprimed baseline + synthetic negatives? numbers? :thinking_face: 

jordana: baseline (no priming): ndcg@10 0.261, mrr 0.184. anchors_B: ndcg@10 0.249, mrr 0.187. So ndcg down, mrr slightly up — looks like top-1 improved at expense of tail.

sam: Could be scoring rescale / tie-handling after quantization. try `score_rescale=0.9` quick.

jordana: tried rescale 0.9 — ndcg@10 recovers to 0.256, mrr 0.186. Looks promising. Will run significance test (paired bootstrap).

ci-bot: build 2026-03-21-1710 completed for r3b-v2-int8. Artifacts at s3://redwood/ci/r3b-v2-int8/20260321

mike: Also run anchor set A (short queries) and mixed anchors; want to see interaction with prefixcache.

jordana: On it. Plan: 1) paired bootstrap 10k samples 2) run with prefixcache disabled 3) compare tokenization differences across anchors

dina: also add a holdout with deduped candidates to control for candidate pool bias.

jordana: noted — will post results later today. Thanks.
